title: Persist Celery execution identity across task lifecycle
description: Persist the dispatched Celery job id for every queued task, expose it through task serialization, and make cancel/reconcile paths use the same durable execution identity.
action: In backend/services/task_service.py, change enqueue_task() so each .delay(str(task.id)) call stores the returned AsyncResult.id into AgentTask.celery_task_id; in backend/tasks/develop_code.py, backend/tasks/deploy.py, and backend/tasks/test.py, persist self.request.id when worker execution starts if celery_task_id is empty; in serialize_task(), include celery_task_id in the returned payload; in cancel_task(), log and revoke the persisted celery_task_id value instead of relying on an empty field.

convergence.definition_of_done: Queued, running, and canceled tasks all refer to the same persisted Celery execution id.

files.change: Store AsyncResult.id in celery_task_id, surface it in serialized task data, and use it in revoke/log flows.
Persist self.request.id into the AgentTask row before running task_service.run_develop_task().
Persist self.request.id into the AgentTask row before calling update_status(TaskStatus.RUNNING).
Persist self.request.id into the AgentTask row before running task_service.run_playwright_smoke_task().
Add enqueue/cancel coverage that asserts celery_task_id is persisted and used for cancel/revoke paths.

implementation: Refactor enqueue_task() to capture the AsyncResult object returned by develop_code_task.delay(), deploy_task.delay(), and smoke_test_task.delay().
Open an async session in enqueue_task() or route the persistence through an async helper so AgentTask.celery_task_id is committed immediately after dispatch.
At the beginning of each Celery task entrypoint, persist self.request.id if the task row still has an empty celery_task_id.
Extend serialize_task() to include celery_task_id so APIs and logs can use the same durable execution identity.
Add pytest coverage in backend/tests/test_task_lifecycle.py for enqueue persistence and cancellation against the stored celery_task_id.

success_metrics: Persisted celery_task_id is non-empty after enqueue
Cancel path revokes the stored id and logs the cancellation request

reference.pattern: Fresh async DB session usage inside Celery workers

rationale.chosen_approach: This is the smallest durable fix that aligns task dispatch, worker execution, and cancel paths without changing queue topology.
decision_factors: AgentTask already has a celery_task_id column
cancel_task() already expects a persisted Celery id
worker entrypoints already own the real execution boundary
rationale.tradeoffs: Requires a small async persistence helper in a synchronous enqueue path, but avoids hidden in-memory state.

risks: Do not block enqueue on long database work; persist only the Celery id and reuse existing session helpers.
